I’ve been farming these 18.8 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. At 65, living alone, I know exactly what my two hands can manage, and I’m not about to gamble on fancy new methods. I’ll keep 15 mu in my wheat–maize rotation—that’s my reliable core. The other 3.8 mu is that drier, sandier corner plot where cotton has always done better than wheat.

My winter wheat went into the ground last October, and now it’s greening up. I’ll run the rotary tiller once to break the crust and top-dress urea at green-up and again at jointing. I’ll irrigate three times from my well—greening, jointing, and grain-filling—and spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect about 450 kg per mu if the weather holds.

Come early June, right after wheat harvest, I’ll immediately no-till sow my summer maize with hybrid seed. Maize is straightforward: base fertilizer at sowing, nitrogen top-dress at the big trumpet stage, two irrigations, and two sprays for corn borer. I can get 550 kg per mu most years.

Cotton is a different story. It’s labor-heavy with all the spraying and hand-picking, so I won’t expand beyond my usual 3.8 mu. I’ll plough that plot deep because cotton likes loose soil, plant improved seed in late April, and give it more phosphorus and potash than the grain crops. It’ll need four irrigations and five pesticide sprays against bollworm. If I harvest 100 kg of seed cotton per mu, I’ll be satisfied.

At my age, I stick with what I know, keep costs down, and make sure I can still do the hand-work myself.
